title: IE exception
hints: Compare the result with each choice and check its sign, units, or underlying rule.
solution: Al loses a 3p electron, which is easier to remove here than Mg’s 3s electron.
statement:
Which has lower first ionization energy, Mg or Al?

[_]{a}

choices: Al, because its first removed electron is in 3p.
Mg, because the trend never reverses.
Al, because it has fewer protons.
They have equal values because both have n=3.
explanations: This is a common across-period exception.
Subshell occupancy can reverse the simple pattern.
Aluminum has more protons than magnesium.
Different subshells and effective attractions matter.
